On Sun, Nov 29, 2026, Julia Ames <julia.ames@acmecloud.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the intro. We're kicking off onboarding for two new vendors (EdgeScale and KestrelOps) that will process telemetry for our managed ML pipelines...

Quick read-through from Legal — overall we can accept the customer request with targeted constraints. Summary of proposed positions:

- Subcontractor approvals: we will not require prior express consent for every downstream subcontractor. Instead, we propose a two-tier model in the MSA amendment:
  * Tier 1 (vendors processing production PII or customer code) — customer notification + 10 business day review window to object; if no objection, notification deemed accepted.
  * Tier 2 (infrastructure/support vendors) — notification only.

- DPA alignment: include a short exhibit referencing Redwood's standard DPA; for vendor-specific treatment (e.g., EdgeScale if they will hold raw telemetry) require a signed subprocessor addendum.

- Audit rights: propose annual audits with remote evidence first; for-cause/on-site audits reserved with prior notice and reasonable scope limitations.

I have redlined language for the MSA and added a 1-paragraph amendment for the Order Form to expressly list known Tier-1 subvendors and to confirm audit cadence. See attached ACME_OrderForm_AMD-1.pdf (redlines).

Next actions I recommend:
1) Dev confirms whether Acme will accept the notification + review window for Tier-1 rather than explicit opt-in.
2) A joint call Dec 1 to walk through redlines (30 min) — Rafael + Aisha + Dev + Julia + Acme procurement.
3) If call agrees, we prepare DocuSign envelope with: MSA Amendment + Order Form AMD + Subvendor list (csv) for signature.

I can finalize language by EOD today if you want to run it by the product team first.

- Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
